mappings.note: Substitution job: m = -v/u fixes u, then 1/v+1/u=1/f gives f. LO-1 would fit only if the answer were the image's position/nature by object-position rule; here the graded step is arithmetic in the two mirror formulae.

Relative refractive index judged from the ray bending away from the normal - the 'defines refractive index / laws of refraction' half of LO-3. Not C 8.1-LO-2: the diagram is given as correct and is not being drawn or judged.
Identifying a rectangular slab from parallel-in/parallel-out beams is the law-of-refraction consequence (lateral shift). No mirror or lens is involved, so the lens/mirror outcomes do not apply.

Identifies a convex lens from converging ray behaviour. LO-3 covers only laws of refraction, refractive index and the lens formula - none is used - so the competency's 'properties of lenses (focus)' clause is the narrowest true fit.
P = 1/f in dioptres. Nearest legal code only: LO-3 is the lens quantitative outcome, but power of a lens appears in no outcome of curriculum 71 (see defect list).

Named quantity is magnification but nothing is substituted; the answer is the standing characteristic of a convex mirror image (always diminished). LO-2 is reserved for items that actually work the magnification formula.
Solved by the object-at-C rule (sun converges at F, so R = 2f = 30 cm), i.e. locating the image by object position, not by substituting into 1/v+1/u=1/f.
Choice of mirror from the field of view and the always-diminished virtual image of a convex mirror - image characteristics, LO-1. No formula and no diagram is produced.
Source at the focus of a concave reflector gives a parallel beam: the reverse of the parallel-ray rule, an image-location fact about concave mirrors.
Object at infinity across all four elements. LO-1 carries the two mirrors; the lens half has no outcome at all in this frame, so the competency is cited for it.
Pure recall of the scope of the laws of reflection - the 'states the laws of reflection' clause of LO-1, with no image being located.

The graded step is judging which of four traced ray paths is correct, so the ray-diagram outcome is cited alongside the law of refraction that decides it. C 8.1-LO-2 names only mirrors and lenses; applied here to a slab by extension.
Ranks four liquids by refractive index to predict which bends light most - the refractive-index clause of LO-3, not a mirror or lens question.
Whole task is picking the correct concave-mirror ray construction (ray towards F reflects parallel to the axis). No image position or formula is asked for, so LO-1/LO-2 are not what is graded.
Same construction test for a lens: the answer is which refracted ray is drawn correctly, which is exactly the ray-diagram outcome rather than any image-finding one.
Maps enlarged/same-size/diminished onto concave/plane/convex - the image characteristics of all three mirror types, which is LO-1's 'plane, concave and convex' clause.
Column matching of object position against image nature for a concave mirror - LO-1. (Item is corrupt as printed; see defect list.)
Turns on whether a convex mirror image is inverted or erect - an image characteristic. No magnification value is computed, so LO-2 does not apply.
Why n > 1 for every medium and air is rarest - the definition of refractive index via speed of light, LO-3's middle clause.
Cause of refraction (differing speeds) - the laws-of-refraction clause of LO-3; nothing about lenses or the lens formula.
Two false claims to separate: the assertion is the R-f relation of a mirror (LO-1), the reason is a ray-construction rule (a parallel ray reflects through F, not C), which is C 8.1-LO-2's territory.
Emergent ray parallel after a slab, and whether differing refractive indices explain it - both clauses sit in LO-3; no diagram is produced.
The reason clause is the magnification formula itself (m = h'/h, not v/u), hence LO-2; the assertion is purely about the sign a real image carries, which is the sign-convention outcome C 5.3-LO-1.
Direction of bending rarer-to-denser and the speed comparison - the laws of refraction, LO-3. Optical density is not a mirror or lens property.

Only physics used is that a convex lens converges. LO-3 requires laws of refraction, refractive index or the lens formula, none of which is invoked, so the competency's lens clause is the honest level.
